idiom_name: hand-written conditional UPDATE (sqlx QueryResult::rows_affected, Diesel execute) or AtomicU64 compare_exchange for in-memory state
implementation_notes: No mainstream Rust ORM ships the counter - SeaORM's optimistic locking is still an open feature request - so the classic structure is written against the query tool you already use: sqlx gives QueryResult::rows_affected() from execute(), and Diesel's update returns the affected rows from .execute(conn) after you add .filter(version.eq(..)) to the query, so 0 is the stale signal in both. For shared in-process state the token is std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64 and compare_exchange is the check, handing back the observed version on failure so the caller can re-read. The token plus predicate is exactly what the ecosystem leaves to you, and the strong typing does not make a statement remember to match the version.
pitfalls: rows_affected() semantics differ by backend (MySQL reports matched rows by default, others changed rows), so state which meaning your 0 has before relying on it.
Holding a transaction open across user think time exhausts the pool; the token exists so the read can finish and the write can re-check - do not keep the transaction alive to compensate.
compare_exchange protects the token only; publish the payload behind an ordering that makes the new data visible when the exchange succeeds.
